directAnswer: To use a passkey, you need to set it up in your device's settings and then use it for authentication when prompted by supported apps or websites.
summary: Passkeys provide a secure and convenient way to authenticate without traditional passwords.

sections.heading: What is a Passkey?
sections.body: A passkey is a cryptographic credential that replaces traditional passwords, allowing for secure authentication across devices and platforms.

sections.heading: Setting Up Passkeys
sections.body: To set up a passkey, navigate to your device's security settings and follow the prompts to create a new passkey.

sections.heading: Using Passkeys for Authentication
sections.body: When logging into a supported service, select the option to use a passkey and follow the on-screen instructions to authenticate.

steps.title: Access Security Settings
steps.detail: Open your device's settings app and navigate to the security section. The path may vary by operating system.

steps.title: Create a Passkey
steps.detail: Select the option to add a new passkey and follow the prompts to create one. Ensure your device is updated to the latest OS version.

steps.title: Authenticate with Passkey
steps.detail: When prompted at a login screen, choose the passkey option and follow the instructions to complete the authentication.

faqs.question: Can I use passkeys on multiple devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, passkeys can be synced across devices if you are using the same account and have enabled sync in your settings.

faqs.question: What happens if I lose my device?
faqs.answer: If you lose your device, you may need to use recovery options provided by your service provider to regain access to your accounts.

faqs.question: Are all websites compatible with passkeys?
faqs.answer: No, not all websites currently support passkeys. Check the website's authentication options for compatibility.

caveats: Passkey support may vary by platform and service provider.
Ensure your device is running the latest software version for optimal compatibility.
